change_log: r2 (2026-11-13): TABLE_RULE steps 3-4 replaced by the per-instance dictionary-derived table-level rule (fail closed for unknown / missing-from-sys_db_object / failed load); added cache_and_refresh. Execute: added sys_variable_value, moved sys_rest_message, sys_rest_message_fn, sys_soap_message to admin, downgraded sp_page and sys_report to write; prefixes: added sys_pd_*, dropped sys_ux_* and the sys_security_*_script placeholder. Admin: removed nonexistent sys_credentials, added privilege tables, password/password2 field rule, replaced the sys_user_* prefix with an exact list, sys_dictionary/sys_db_object exact-only, sys_properties all keys. Fixed SN-Create-Activity (script goes to wf_activity.input) and SN-Create-Workflow (condition is `conditions`; on_cancel is the script) notes. sys_ws_definition and ecc_agent left as OPEN owner questions. Per-tool access classes unchanged (29 read / 23 write / 6 execute / 2 admin).

class_definitions.read: no state change on instance or server (picker/instance reads count as read)
class_definitions.write: creates/updates instance data or config via the Table/UI APIs, or writes bounded local server files; cannot cause caller-chosen code to run
class_definitions.execute: can run code on the instance: caller-supplied scripts, writes to script-bearing/scheduler tables or script-typed fields, activation of stored scripts, or dispatch of stored test code (ATF)
class_definitions.admin: mutates MCP-server configuration or process-wide shared state, or (via TABLE_RULE) writes privilege/schema/credential tables

output_definitions.record-data: anything derived from instance row content or caller-chosen queries (incl. free text, user-authored rows, script output) - subject to DataProtector
output_definitions.metadata: schema, definitions, configuration, status of instance/server; no business-row content
output_definitions.static-public: content from public docs or packaged static files only; no instance data

meta.hints_note: readOnlyHint/destructiveHint/idempotentHint/openWorldHint are advisory MCP annotations (spec 2026-07-28 tool annotations). NEVER used for policy; policy uses access/escalation. Fixture 6.2.0 carries no annotations at all, so these are all new.
meta.hints_derivation: readOnly = access read AND side_effect none. destructive = tool overwrites existing values (updates/state changes/script execution) vs purely additive. idempotent = repeated call with same args leaves same state (value-wise; side effects like notifications ignored). openWorld = contacts ServiceNow or GitHub (any external system); false for local-only.
meta.output_class_note: `output_class` is the legacy D05 vocabulary (record-data|metadata|static-public|none) kept only for its justification text. `dp_output_class` (none|schema|records|opaque) is canonical; see output-class-vocabulary.md.
meta.dp_output_class_derivation: record-data -> records, except script output / logs / CI-CD / ATF JSON -> opaque; metadata -> schema; static-public and none -> none. `none` applies to successful results only; error, progress and log channels are never none (DP schema N4).

table_rule.statement: effective_class = max(base_class, class(table), class(fields written), class(values written)); order read < write < execute < admin. Batch tools take the max over every operation. Mismatch with the principal's granted class => deny before any HTTP call.
steps: 1. Normalize table: trim, lowercase; reject anything not matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,79}$ (Node accepts arbitrary strings for Query-Table/Create-Record/Update-Record; SN-Update-Record builds /api/now/table/${table}/${sysId} unvalidated, src/mcp-server-consolidated.js:1686). sys_id must match ^[0-9a-f]{32}$.

2. Resolve ancestors via sys_db_object.super_class chain (cached per instance; see "Cache and refresh"). class(table) = max over the table and all ancestors, except admin tables listed as exact-only below. FAIL CLOSED to execute if resolution fails, the table is unknown, or the table is missing from sys_db_object (e.g. var__m_* variable tables, which are not registered there; evidence: exec-table-verification.md section 2b and Unknowns).

3. Per-instance dictionary-derived execute class (replaces the former static-lookup and field-rule steps; evidence and rationale: exec-table-verification.md sections 2d, 3, 4). At connect, build exec_tables for the instance as the closure over the sys_db_object.super_class chain of (a) every table with a sys_dictionary field whose internal_type is in {script, script_plain, script_server, script_client, html_script, email_script, condition, condition_string, expression, formula, xml, html_template, workflow_conditions, glide_var, data_object} and (b) every table with a string-typed field named script, onclick, calculation, function_definition, dynamic_creation_script or ending _script (always applied, not only as a fallback). glide_script and javascript are kept only as forward aliases (0 fields on PDI dev451274). The rule is TABLE-level: ANY write to a table in exec_tables is execute, whichever field is written, because non-script fields (active, advanced, when, order, run_as) change which code runs.

4. Static union and fail-closed: execute also applies to the static carriers/containers and prefixes listed below. Unknown table, table missing from sys_db_object, or a failed/unavailable dictionary load => every table outside the static lists is execute (FAIL CLOSED); a field-name filter is never trusted as a substitute because it cannot find unknown names. Expected false positives (XML-only tables such as sys_soap_message_test, logs such as sys_script_execution_history, runtime glide_var holders) are accepted; business-data tables (task, cmdb_ci, ...) stay write.

5. Value rule: any written string value whose trimmed text starts with "javascript:" (reference qualifiers, dynamic defaults, dynamic filters) or contains "<g:evaluate" / "${" Jelly/script markers => execute.

6. sys_update_xml / sys_remote_update_set: writing payload/name/type/action/target_name => execute (committing/previewing applies arbitrary records incl. scripts); writing ONLY the update_set pointer (SN-Move-Records-To-Update-Set) => write.

7. Privilege/credential tables => admin (proposed; owner decision 3): the exact list and prefixes below, plus any table (own or inherited field) with a sys_dictionary internal_type of password or password2 (73 tables excluding var__m_* on PDI dev451274; exec-table-verification.md section 4). class = max over ancestors, except sys_dictionary and sys_db_object, which match exact-only (otherwise the 60 var_dictionary-derived variable tables would become admin; default applied, owner may override). sys_properties: every write is admin, with no key pattern matching.
8. Delete is not exposed by any of the 60 tools; if added later it must carry its own rule.
execute_tables_exact: sys_ws_definition (OPEN owner question: container routing to sys_ws_operation scripts; keep execute or downgrade to write)
item_option_new (default/qualifier scripts; also covered by field+value rules)
ecc_queue (Command/JavascriptProbe topics execute on a MID server)
ecc_agent (OPEN owner question: MID metadata only; execute, admin or write)
sys_data_source (also has password2, so resolves to admin via the credential rule)
admin_tables_exact: sys_properties (all keys; no key pattern matching)
table_rule.admin_field_rule: internal_type `password` or `password2` => admin (any table, own or inherited field). Covers credential tables absent from the exact list (for example sys_email_account, ldap_server_config, sys_soap_message_function, sys_wss_profile, gen_ai_service_secret; full list: exec-table-verification.md section 4). `sys_generated_security_acl` and the other sys_security_acl descendants are admin by propagation, `sys_auth_policy_*` by the `sys_auth_*` prefix. `sys_credentials` does not exist on the PDI and was removed; the `sys_user_*` prefix (36 tables, mostly non-privilege such as sys_user_preference, sys_user_session, sys_user_login_history) was replaced by the exact list.
cache_and_refresh: Cache per instance, never the full dictionary (about 15 MB, about 17 requests, about 2.7 min). Cache only the sys_dictionary subset (the step 3 type set, password/password2 fields, and the string-name heuristic) plus the sys_db_object name/super_class parent map: about 1.1 MB, 4 requests, roughly 15 s cold on the PDI (the string-name query dominates).
Key the cache by instance + glide.war + the max sys_updated_on of sys_dictionary and sys_db_object.
Refresh on miss: an unknown table triggers a re-query of sys_db_object name=<t> and sys_dictionary name=<t>; the result is cached. Also apply a TTL (default 24 h).

Failed load, or a table still unknown after a refresh, fails closed to execute (step 4). On the PDI, 37 sys_db_object rows are invisible to admin over REST (cause unknown); tables among them would fail closed.

open_owner_questions.question: Container that routes inbound calls to sys_ws_operation scripts; it has no script field itself. Keep execute or downgrade to write?
Holds MID metadata only (no script field). Options: admin if MID trust/validation is the concern, otherwise write. How validation is performed is [INFERENCE].

table_rule.verification_status: Table lists VERIFIED read-only against PDI dev451274 (Australia patch 3) on 2026-11-13: exec-table-verification.md (564 script-bearing tables found; the former static execute list covered only 129 of them, which is why steps 3-4 are dictionary-derived). table_rule.read_side_note: Read class never escalates by table, but reading sensitive tables (sys_user, sys_properties password2, any table matching the admin field rule, oauth_credential, ecc_queue, sys_update_xml payload, sys_email, syslog) must hand off to DataProtector (D06) as record-data.
